title: Strategic plan midway check-in and public art
subtitle: Idlewood Greenway funding, affordable housing tax exemption, and a mosaic for the new indoor recreation complex
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended changes to the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan after a midway check-in. Two recreation projects, the Sport and Recreation Master Plan and the City-led Recreation & Leisure Program Review, would be referred to the 2027-2030 plan rather than removed. Two items would be added: a Make it Kitchener 2.0 refresh and implementation of the Downtown Safety & Security Action Plan {{vote:m3}}.

The committee also recommended moving $5.36M in 2026 funding from the Middle Strasburg Naturalization project to the Idlewood Greenway, with early tender approval in 2025 {{vote:m1}}. It recommended a City property tax exemption for affordable housing units at 475-477 Lancaster Street West {{vote:m2}}.

The committee recommended commissioning the artwork "Gidinawendimin" for the new Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex at RBJ Schlegel Park {{vote:m4}}. Because these are committee recommendations, Council must still adopt them. Residents may see changes to recreation planning timelines, downtown safety work and a major new public art piece.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended referring two recreation projects to the 2027-2030 plan, adding the Make it Kitchener 2.0 refresh and Downtown Safety & Security Action Plan implementation, and directing staff on social resilience, Lean training, Innovation Lab projects and better indicators.
The committee recommended reallocating $5.36M of 2026 funding from the Middle Strasburg Naturalization project to the Idlewood Greenway and preapproving it for tender in 2025.

The committee recommended a by-law exempting qualifying units at 475-477 Lancaster Street West from the City's portion of the property tax levy through the Region's Municipal Housing Facility program.

The committee recommended approving the commission and installation of "Gidinawendimin" at the new indoor recreation complex, and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign an agreement with the artist's representative.

debate: On the two recreation projects, one councillor asked whether delay to 2027 would leave current needs unmet. Staff said they knew of no imminent gap and that project staff had been reassigned to open the new recreation complex.
The Mayor preferred "refer" over "remove" so the projects stay visible and accountable, though the next Council could reverse it. Staff said they were saying similar things.

On the downtown safety plan, one councillor asked whether the City might take on work belonging to other levels of government. Staff said the Region, police and BIA are partners and the City is facilitating. The Downtown Safety Ambassador Program was named as the most costly City item, partly BIA-funded.

Councillors discussed the social resilience theme, including integrating newcomers, volunteering, and responding to anti-immigrant comments. Others raised economic uncertainty from tariffs and the use of AI to improve productivity.

On the artwork, staff said the original competition closed because the facility design changed, and the jury then recommended an invited commission for the aquatic centre. One councillor noted the process did not follow the public art policy exactly and asked for a cost breakdown, which staff agreed to share. Others praised the piece and its value.
